✂ ISOLATE A PART · run just a selection, at fine grid
Simulating: whole model. Draw a tight box around just the part you care about — one apartment, a courtyard, a façade bay — and only that is solved, at a finer grid (the cell size auto-refines to the small area; for sub-metre detail use the Cavity resolution preset). The rest of the model is not simulated.
◱▸▪ Study in context (nested)
Solves the whole model once at a coarse grid to capture the real wind arriving at your selection, then solves just the selection at a fine grid using that as its inflow — instead of a uniform wind at the crop edge. Use it when upstream buildings shelter or funnel wind toward your zone. Skip it when the selection sits in open flow (a plain crop is identical and faster). Keep the crop edge a few metres clear of buildings; the coarse pass must converge; GPU Turbo is off during the two passes (slower).

Isolate + safety
Sweep runs on: whole model. Isolate one dwelling / bay to sweep just that part, at a finer grid.
Three ways to run many winds — which one?
1 · Run wind directions (top bar) — quick screen of 8 directions to find the worst. Nothing is kept.
2 · Simulate all typical winds (below) — full runs of this site's real ERA5 winds, kept so you can read each back.
3 · Build & run campaign (below) — sweep direction × speed × porosity to compare design variants (table + CSV).
SETUP · settings + views, no model
A setup is every setting plus every saved view — a few kB, with no geometry and no results. Save your method once and apply it to any other model. (A full project with the model is SAVE STUDIO.)
RUNS · every typical wind, kept
Solves every typical wind of this site in turn and keeps each result whole (field + metrics + the weather moment). Without this, each run overwrites the last. Click a stored run to read it back.
A stored field is the whole lattice — on a tight site ~50 MB per run. They live in memory for the session; Save runs offers a light (metrics-only) file.

Help — wind & ventilation for architects

A fast wind-study tool. It shows how wind moves around and through your buildings - for comfort, ventilation and shelter. A design-screening aid, not a certified report.

① The quick path — 5 moves through the numbered menus

  1. Bring in geometry — 4 Import geometry into site (▲ 3DM/OBJ from Rhino/SketchUp, or a DXF plan). Or start from 1 Site to load the OpenStreetMap surroundings, or 3 Draw massing on site to sketch by hand.
  2. Pick the area to study — ✂ Select area (drag a box over the part you care about). Smaller area = finer detail.
  3. Set the wind — 2 Weather pulls the real ERA5 wind for a chosen moment; fine-tune the vector on the compass rose in 6 Wind analysis.
  4. Give each object its role — 5 Characterize: Solid (wind goes around), Permeable (porous façades / screens — set the porosity %), Vegetation (porous + cooling), or Void / Opening (a hole for cross-vent).
  5. ▶ Run (8 Simulation) — read the colours + flow lines; Section tab = the vertical (elevation) study; 11 Results interpretation explains the numbers.

② How to prepare the model

  • Units in metres. Model real size; the tool auto-detects mm/cm if needed.
  • OBJ from Rhino/SketchUp: keep each building as its own object/group; export File → Export → .obj. Trees as separate round/squat objects (read as vegetation).
  • Keep it clean: only the massing you want in the wind — delete furniture, people, tiny details, interior clutter. Closed/solid volumes work best.
  • DXF plan: walls on a clear layer; windows/doors on their own layer (used as openings). You assign each layer on import.
  • Orientation: if it imports turned, use ⟳ Orient model (↺ 90° / fine slider). Check the N arrow.
  • Heavy model? ✂ Select area first — then the chosen zone runs fine and sharp.

③ What the words mean

  • Resolution (m/cell) — the grid fineness. Smaller = sharper + slower. Auto-size picks a good value; it shows right after you import.
  • Arrows — wind direction + strength at a grid of points. Streamlines — continuous lines following the wind. Contours — lines of equal speed (like map contours). Silky — a brushed texture showing flow everywhere.
  • Colour shows — Wind speed / Pressure / Temperature / Comfort / Swirl (eddies at corners & wakes).
  • Domain — the box of air simulated around your site. Blockage ≤ 10% = good proportion (raise the margin if higher).
  • Porosity % — how OPEN a permeable material is: high = airy screen, low = nearly solid.

④ Reading the results — what's good?

  • Mean wind — average speed in your area. Compared to the open free-stream, ~50–70% means the buildings shelter the wind without killing it. Too high = draughty, too low = stuffy.
  • Stagnation — % of the area with nearly still air (<0.3 m/s) — the dead corners. Aim below ~20%; above ~35% the layout traps stale, hot air.
  • Façade wind exposure — how much wind reaches the building fronts, as a % of the open wind. 50%+ = well exposed (good for natural ventilation); a big upwind→downwind drop means the rear buildings sit in the wind shadow.
  • Adaptive comfort — % of the area where people would feel comfortable, given the air temperature and the cooling effect of the wind we simulated. Green/“Good” ≈ 70%+. Switch the colour field to Comfort to see WHERE (green = comfortable, red = too warm).
  • Converging % — the solver settling into a steady answer; 100% = ready to read. Watch the live narrative under the progress bar.
  • → Design moves — after a run, the results box suggests what to change (open a gap, add trees, vent the rear). Use 📌 Pin to compare to test two options side by side.
Worked example. A 4-storey courtyard block, summer SW wind: mean wind 1.4 m/s (60% sheltered — fine), stagnation 28% (a bit high), façade wind 70% upwind but 18% downwind (rear in deep shadow), comfort 55% (mixed). Read it as: the courtyard is calm but the back flats won't cross-ventilate and afternoons are warm. Design move: open a gap in the windward wall to push air into the courtyard, and add shade trees — then Pin & re-Run to confirm comfort rises.

Under the hood: a 2D Lattice-Boltzmann wind solver (horizontal plan + vertical section), Smagorinsky turbulence model, wind profile with height. It runs at a reduced (numerical) Reynolds number on a single slice — screening accuracy: use it to compare options, not to certify absolute numbers. Comfort uses air temperature + wind only (no solar/MRT/humidity), so outdoors in the sun it reads optimistic.

Turbulence model keep On
Adds realistic small-scale mixing to the wind so results are steadier and more lifelike (Smagorinsky LES, Cs 0.12). Off = smooth laminar flow — a deliberate test only. Re-run after changing.
Ready · est. 15s
ETA appears after the first solver chunks.
Press ▶ Run — the wind solver iterates until the flow stops changing (converges).
Convergence check0%
Run the simulation to measure residual and result readiness.
Look for: settling >= 95%, KE drift below 2e-5 per step for 3 chunks, and a flat kinetic-energy tail.

Expert commentary
Reads the weather comfort band, the useful-ventilation analysis and the CFD results together, and writes an interpretive commentary. Runs on demand, or automatically inside the report.
⚙ Text-service endpoint & key — optional (stored locally in your browser)
Endpoint Model API key
OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint. Default: Pollinations (get a pk_ key at enter.pollinations.ai). Your key never leaves your browser — it is stored in localStorage and sent only to the endpoint you set.
Report after simulation▾
This builds a multi-page PNG study document — one landscape page per view and per weather period (ISO + plan, annotated with the weather and CFD status). Choose which periods and views in Report settings, then press Build + save PNGs.
The two headline readings printed on every page
Adaptive thermal comfort (EN 16798-1) — % of the zone inside the thermal band; higher is better.
Pedestrian wind (Lawson / NEN-8100) — wind class by gust. The campaign's calm / walkable / windy split = <1 / 1–4 / >4 m/s.
4 periods · 8 image pages + cover

◱ Discretize complex volume → massing
Replace a heavy/complex shape with a light, precise stepped massing (voxel height-field). Keeps the real footprint, per-column height and courtyards; strips interior clutter. Recommended before a whole-site wind run.
1 m
Finer = more precise + tighter footprint (heavier). 1 m is the validated sweet spot (~100× lighter, surface fully contained).
